page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is a high clock speed compute instance configured on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a 3.1 GHz base frequency. The processor features 35 MB of shared L3 cache and supports AVX-512 instruction extensions, including VNNI. System memory is provisioned at 128 GB, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Storage and acceleration tradeoffs define the platform boundary. The instance contains zero local disk storage, requiring external cloud storage volumes for operating system disks and persistent file data. Hardware accelerators are not included, meaning GPU-dependent workloads are unsupported, though vector extensions provide baseline capability for smaller CPU-based inference tasks. Networking is provisioned with a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth allocation.

Benchmark measurements reflect uniform compute and memory throughput. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 29517.51 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11107.0, with a single-core score of 1287.0. Memory subsystems registered 109.89 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 48.22 GB/sec for write operations. In workload-specific testing, the server processed 28.91 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 21.45 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The ecs.hfg6.8xlarge provides dedicated CPU allocation without resource sharing penalties, making it cost-efficient for sustained execution rather than bursty low-priority loads. The instance profile is suited for continuous integration build farms, distributed in-memory caching tiers, high-concurrency web application backends, and relational database services attached to network storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is a high clock speed virtual machine driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. Configured on KVM virtualization, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 35 MB of L3 cache, and 128 GB of memory, maintaining a 4 GB per vCPU ratio. The platform includes AVX-512 extensions but features no discrete GPUs or bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage and operating over a 10 Gbps baseline network link. Empirical benchmark results show steady compute execution with a Geekbench multi-core score of 11107.0, a PassMark CPU score of 29517.51, and large-block read memory bandwidth of 109.89 GB/sec. Synthetic application benchmarks report 28.91 million Redis SET operations per second and 21.45 GB/sec static web throughput. This instance matches compute-bound tasks including software compilation, in-memory caching layers, enterprise application serving, and network-backed database hosting.
